set.body:
Split from P6f.12 on 2026-08-03, following the P6f.30 precedent of carving an
immediately-actionable subset out of that bead while full codec ownership stays there.

WHY SPLIT. P6f.12 is still blocked by P6f.23 (typed pre-deadline signal support), and
that block is legitimate for two of its acceptance criteria: hand-owning every field name
and pinning every golden fixture while a new JobRequest field is still inbound would mean
doing the work twice. It is NOT legitimate for the property-law criterion. Laws are
written against whatever field set exists and keep passing as fields are added; that is
the point of them. P6f.23 adding a field later is precisely the event these laws should
catch if a codec forgets it.

THE REGRESSION THIS CLOSES, quoted from the P6f.12 evidence note of 2026-08-03: the
exhaustive audit found exactly one silently dropped field, JobObservation.reportedCluster,
and the reason it was invisible is the general problem. The field has a default, so the
decoder could construct the type with eight of nine arguments and still typecheck under
-Werror, and no fixture or property pinned the field set. The audit was a one-time
snapshot and cannot prevent recurrence. A round-trip law over generated values is the only
check that fails automatically when the next defaulted field is added, and it applies to
every hand-written codec over a type with defaulted fields.

Unblocked by P7.2: with one byte representation the laws are written once rather than
rewritten after a representation swap. That was the stated reason to sequence P7.2 first.

Scope and acceptance:
- Generators for the protocol types the hand-written codecs serialize, built on the
  existing core Generators rather than duplicating them.
- Round-trip law decode(encode(x)) == Right(x) for the hand-written pairs in
  AgentDomainJson, StructuredResultCodec, AgentMessageCodec, ControlCommandJson and
  FileJournalControlStore.JournalCodec. A generated value must be able to populate every
  defaulted field, otherwise the law cannot see the bug class it exists to catch.
- Malformed-input law: no decoder throws on arbitrary or structurally wrong JSON; every
  failure arrives as a Left.
- Bounds law plus the fix for the concrete asymmetry recorded on P6f.12: decodeRemoteBoundedEvidence
  bounds base64 before allocating via decodeBase64Bounded, but Decoder[BoundedEvidence] and
  Decoder[LogPage] via decodeBase64 decode straight into an unbounded array, and resultRefs
  is decoded with no cardinality cap. Frame-level maximumFrameBytes is the only thing
  bounding them today, so this is defence-in-depth, not a live overflow.

Explicitly NOT in scope, remaining on P6f.12: renaming to owned stable field names and
discriminator values, language-neutral golden fixtures for every agent method, and
compatibility ownership of intentional format changes.
set.title: P6f.34: Prove round-trip, malformed-input and bounds laws for the hand-written codecs
